CHAPTER 6  
CONCLUSIONS / FUTURE WORK 
6.1 Conclusions 
The project implemented a range of features including a comprehensive 
achievements system, completive leader board system, spaced-repetition, and a 
scalable short-from content delivery platform, reaching up to task 41 in Table 
27. However, it lacked a diverse range of question types, as highlighted by the 
participants within the study. This limitation failed to address one of the 
identified issues within existing solutions. Despite this the project successfully 
aligned with the initial aims and objects, by developing an eLearning application 
that enhanced engagement and content mastery among GCSE students. 
The project held a strong focus on the defined aims throughout research and 
development. However, the project experienced minor scope creep following the 
literature review within Chapter 2, resulting in the inclusion of additional 
features such as leader boards and spaced repetition. These additional features, 
while initially unplanned for, emerged as a suitable natural fit, building upon the 
authors gained knowledge. Ultimately these features benefited the applications 
performance and enhanced its overall quality and polish. 
The findings from Chapter 5 address this research gaps identified within Chapter 
2, regarding quantitative analysis of learning outcomes using short-form content 
within the GCSE sciences. By utilising gamified short-from content delivery 
systems, integrating high-level questions and spaced-repetition, the research 
study tests these strategies in practice and provides empirical evidence towards 
their effectiveness among GCSE students.
